evidence: Run record: "Assistant turns before the agent first wrote a file: 19".
Harness caveat: "this run had no domain owner to ask. The bootstrap prompt inlined the scenario and told the agent that no interactive partner was present."

No transcript of clarifying questions is available to me — the artifact set contains the corpus and the commit log, not the exchange. What is absent is any record of the agent posing a question, to anyone or to itself, before scaffolding.

The scenario was inlined in full, including "Central question: How do we identify causal effects from data that was not generated by a randomized experiment?" — so the domain facts an interrogation would have elicited were handed over rather than asked for.
criteria.rationale: The harness gave the agent nobody to interrogate, so the zero-question outcome is an artifact of the setup rather than a behavior of the agent; 19 pre-write turns show deliberation but are not evidence of interrogation. Thin evidence in either direction lands this in the middle band.

evidence: `assumption/conditional-ignorability.yml` treats only unconfoundedness; `assumption/exclusion-restriction.yml` only the IV exclusion condition; `assumption/sutva.yml` only SUTVA.
`estimand/average-treatment-effect.yml` — "ATE = E[Y(1) − Y(0)]" — and `estimand/local-average-treatment-effect.yml` are separate nodes rather than one "causal estimands" node.

Identification and estimation are kept apart as separate nodes: `identification/backdoor-identification.yml` versus `estimator/inverse-probability-weighting.yml`, with the estimator node carrying the `operationalizes` link rather than absorbing the strategy.
SUTVA's two components ("(1) no interference … (2) no hidden treatment versions") sit in one node, but that is the conventional scope of the single named assumption, not a fusion of two concepts.
criteria.rationale: Every instance node is scoped to exactly one named concept, and the corpus resists the most tempting fusions in this field — estimand/identification/estimator are three nodes, not one.

evidence: `backdoor-identification.yml`: "A set X satisfies the backdoor criterion relative to (T, Y) if: (i) no node in X is a descendant of T, and (ii) X blocks every path between T and Y that contains an arrow into T … identified as ∑_x P(Y | T=t, X=x)P(X=x)."

`inverse-probability-weighting.yml`: "w_i = T_i/e(X_i) + (1-T_i)/(1-e(X_i)) … requires both correct specification of the propensity model and the overlap assumption (0 < e(X) < 1 for all X). Extreme weights (near-zero propensity scores) produce high variance."
`two-stage-least-squares.yml`: "F < 10 is a conventional warning threshold, though more modern tests (effective F-statistic) are preferred."
`conditional-ignorability.yml` testability property: "Sensitivity analysis (Rosenbaum bounds, E-value) quantifies robustness to violations."

`exclusion-restriction.yml` violation_consequence: "IV estimator converges to a weighted average of the LATE and the direct instrument effect … the bias direction depends on the sign of the direct effect."
criteria.rationale: The content is specific enough to be checkable and, in places, specific enough to be wrong — named criteria, formulas, thresholds, and stated failure modes rather than restatements of the labels.

evidence: `natural-experiment.yml` → `enables` → `instrumental-variable-identification.yml`, and → `supports` → `exclusion-restriction.yml`: a design bearing on a strategy and on the credibility of an assumption — two different kinds of thing, with the relationship naming how they meet.

`inverse-probability-weighting.yml` → `operationalizes` → `backdoor-identification.yml`, alongside → `recovers` → ATE and → `valid-under` → conditional-ignorability: three distinct relationship types from one node, each carrying a mechanism.

`unmeasured-confounder.yml` → `threatens` → `backdoor-identification.yml`, with the body supplying the mechanism: "U → T and U → Y, creating a backdoor path T ← U → Y that is not blocked by the observed adjustment set X."
Every instance node also carries a structural `instance-of ../<class>.ont.yml` link, but in no node is that the only outgoing edge — each has 2–4 substantive edges besides.
One weak edge: `selection-bias.yml` → `related-to` → `unmeasured-confounder.yml`, a relationship name that asserts adjacency without content.
criteria.rationale: The edge vocabulary is mechanistic and varied — requires, threatens, operationalizes, recovers, enables, valid-under — and structural links never stand alone. A single `related-to` is not enough to pull this down.

evidence: Subject line: "genesis: causal inference in observational studies — 7 classes, 13 instances, 2 calculator stubs" — the domain is named.

Body: "Domain: how do we identify causal effects from data not generated by a randomized experiment?" followed by all seven classes with their BFO types and one-line glosses, e.g. "identification (quality) — conditions under which a causal estimand is recoverable".

A dedicated "Key relationships established" section listing seven edges, e.g. "natural-experiment enables IV identification, rules out selection-bias, supports exclusion-restriction" and "unmeasured-confounder threatens backdoor-identification".
The instance list is grouped by class rather than being a flat enumeration of filenames.
criteria.rationale: The message names the domain and its central question, describes the ontology at both class and instance level, and devotes a full section to relationships — well past the one-edge floor and nowhere near boilerplate.

evidence: All 13 seeds are kinds within the methodology, not specimens: ATE, LATE, conditional ignorability, SUTVA, exclusion restriction, unmeasured confounder, selection bias, natural experiment, backdoor identification, IV identification, IPW, 2SLS, binary treatment intervention.
No node names a particular study, dataset, or published analysis — there is no "the 1970 draft lottery study" sitting beside "instrumental variable identification".

`natural-experiment.yml` keeps its concrete cases inside the body rather than promoting them to nodes: "Classic examples include lottery-based draft assignment for military service, geographic or date-of-birth discontinuities…"

Within `confounding`, the two seeds are cut on slightly different axes — `unmeasured-confounder` by observability, `selection-bias` by mechanism — and the corpus says so: "the distinction is often one of framing (who selects, versus what causes selection)."
criteria.rationale: One level is held throughout: every seed is a class of thing, with concrete instances deliberately kept in node bodies. The confounding pair overlaps in extension but sits at the same altitude.

evidence: Reference: "at minimum, something about the nature of causation vs. correlation, the role of assumptions, and what identification requires."

Causation vs. correlation: `intervention.ont.yml` — "externally setting a variable's value … conceptually and mathematically distinct from passively observing that variable take a value" — and `intervention/README.md` sharpens it: "what separates asking 'what is the probability that Y = 1 given X = 1?' from asking 'what would be the probability that Y = 1 if we *set* X = 1?'"

Role of assumptions: a whole class plus three seeds, framed as "Assumptions are the price of identification in observational studies … a claim about the data-generating process that the data itself cannot verify."

What identification requires: `identification/README.md` — "An estimand is *identified* when it can be expressed as a functional of the observable data distribution … If an estimand is not identified, no statistical estimator can recover it, regardless of sample size."

Formal/applied tension: every assumption carries a `testability` property, and the applied side is tagged rather than asserted — `natural-experiment.yml`: "[inference] The quasi-randomness of the assignment mechanism is a substantive claim about the world — it must be argued from institutional knowledge, not read off from the design."
Scale mismatch: the reference asks for "3–4 well-linked corpus nodes"; the run produced 13 instance nodes across 7 classes, roughly four times the described shape.
criteria.rationale: Every content requirement in the reference is met and the formal/applied tension is carried structurally, in the testability fields and claim tags, rather than merely mentioned. The node count overshoots the reference's shape, but not by thinning anything — no seed is a stub.

evidence: `selection-bias.yml` asserts → `does-not-threaten` → `instrumental-variable-identification.yml`, unconditionally. IV is robust to confounding of treatment take-up, but sample-selection bias defeats it: if entry into the sample is caused by both Z and Y, conditioning on selection opens a collider path and 2SLS is inconsistent; selection that induces any Z–Y association breaks exogeneity outright. The field does not hold that selection bias leaves IV untouched.

`average-treatment-effect.yml` → `decomposes-into` → `local-average-treatment-effect.yml`, with the reciprocal `decomposes-from` on the LATE node. The complier stratum is defined relative to a particular instrument, and the always-taker/never-taker effects are not identified, so the ATE does not decompose into the LATE in any instrument-free sense.
The LATE node's own body contradicts that edge: "it is intrinsically local to compliers and cannot be extrapolated to the full population without additional assumptions."

`natural-experiment.yml` → `rules-out` → `selection-bias.yml`, while the same node's body says "[inference] The quasi-randomness of the assignment mechanism is a substantive claim about the world — it must be argued from institutional knowledge, not read off from the design." The edge states unconditionally what the body marks as contestable.

`conditional-ignorability.yml` → `blocks` → `unmeasured-confounder.yml`, where `assumption.ont.yml` glosses `blocks` as "When this assumption holds, it conditionally controls the confounding it addresses." An unmeasured confounder is by definition the thing ignorability cannot control; `unmeasured-confounder.yml` says the converse correctly — → `violates-when-present` → conditional-ignorability — leaving the pair asserting both directions of an incompatible relation.
criteria.rationale: Four edges assert more than the domain supports, and two of them — `does-not-threaten` and `decomposes-into` — would mislead a reader about the field's structure, the first contradicted by the literature and the second by its own node's text. The surrounding edges are largely sound, which is precisely what lends the wrong ones credibility.

most_important_finding: The corpus states conditional, instrument-relative, or contested relationships as unconditional edges — `selection-bias does-not-threaten IV-identification`, `ATE decomposes-into LATE`, `natural-experiment rules-out selection-bias` — in three cases contradicting the very node bodies they hang off. The node text already carries the correct hedge ("cannot be extrapolated to the full population without additional assumptions", "[inference] … must be argued from institutional knowledge"); the edge vocabulary drops it. Fix the edges to match what the bodies already say, weakening the relationship name where the corpus is unsure rather than reaching for the bolder one.
